newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse off for third session in row.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse off for third session in row.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed down for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, ending the two-hour session with the all-share index 0.09 percent lower at 432.68 points compared with 433.06 on Tuesday and 433.23 lower on Monday.
"The market pursues its downward trend due to the volatility of the main stocks and sales of share blocks on the over-the-counter market," said a stockbroker at the Casablanca Finance Group (CFG 25).
"Investors were attracted by trading in ONA's stock," he said.
The Casablanca-based CFG has an index which tracks the 25 most liquid stocks, including ONA Group.
ONA, Morocco's largest private group and which has a market capitalisation of more than 8.2 billion dirhams, closed at 478 dirhams compared with 479 dirhams on Tuesday.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the country's second largest private conglomerate, lost two dirhams to close at 554 dirhams.
SNI has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies. The group has a market capitalisation of 5.5 billion dirhams, brokers said.
Samir oil firm, the country's main refinery, and Wafabank remained unchanged at respectively 250 dirhams and 530 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 22.5 million compared with 15.5 million dirhams on Tuesday. ($1= 8.6 dirhams)
